html:
A narrow lane in the City of London where share dealing grew up in the coffee houses from the late 1600s. It was the forerunner of the London Stock Exchange.

Dealers in shares and government debt first worked in the Royal Exchange, but their noisy manners got them thrown out around 1698. They moved to coffee houses in the alley nearby, above all Jonathan's and Garraway's. At Jonathan's, John Castaing began printing lists of share and currency prices, one of the first regular price lists.

The alley copied methods first worked out in the Amsterdam Exchange: trading shares, buying on time and betting on prices. Its main stocks were the East India Company, the Bank of England and the South Sea Company. In 1720 the alley was the heart of the South Sea Bubble, when share prices soared and then crashed.

In 1773 the brokers moved into their own building nearby and called it the Stock Exchange. The alley still exists as a passage between Lombard Street and Cornhill.
sum: A narrow lane in the City of London where share dealing grew up in the coffee houses from the late 1600s. It was the forerunner of the London Stock Exchange.
